ti: bench fixture v2: multi-dir rules inventory so text-surface changes measure at real magnitude

note: Fixture v2 shipped: four source dirs (api, api/handlers, store, cli) with compilable files, seven lint-clean rules seeded through the real tool surface in an unmetered phase; scripted steps unchanged, all eight states still covered by construction; report totals labeled fixture=v2 and not comparable to v1. Magnitude acceptance exceeded: the state-collapse change class measures -87B and -103B on the two state calls (-143B net vs the pre-collapse binary) where v1 saw -17B — a 10x sensitivity gain toward the real repository magnitude. Acceptance criterion 3 amended with cause: self-A/B is not exactly 0B because time-ordered IDs give adaptive display prefixes that can differ by a character between runs; measured floor ±2B, and the verdict now says tie-within-noise instead of claiming wins inside it. Two harness defects found and fixed while measuring: the A/B section headers now NAME the binaries in each slot, and a -baseline flag allows benching two foreign builds under the current script — both born from a live sign inversion: bench -against makes the ARGUMENT the candidate, and the B-01KYDS archive note recorded its delta inverted as a result. Erratum for the B-01KYDS record: the true delta is +49B systematic on the archive step, not -49B — and the corrected measurement exposed the real cause, the offline forge Ready never persists the draft flip (recorded as B-01KYDV with isolated cause and fix). Coverage tests green including the new multi-dir clean-inventory pin

ti: agent-judge stage: bench prepares a metered fixture and brief for an independent agent and scores its run mechanically

note: bench gains the stage-4 judge machinery: -agent-prep DIR writes the seeded v2 fixture, a fixed zero-coaching brief (tool names only — semantics must come from the texts under judgment; goals: task agent judge run archived, bug bogus report rejected, check ok), and a metering shim appending bytes, exit and argv per call; -agent-score DIR sums the meter, judges goal states through the public tool surface (find scope=history for the archive event, scope=rejection for the reject snapshot — work.md is the wrong source, archived and rejected items tombstone into the journal, which the first scorer draft learned the hard way), applies the E/W taxonomy to a final check, and exits non-zero when goals are missed. Agent spawning stays outside the repository by design so brief and fixture are identical across builds. Unit test drives the full loop through the shim: prep shape, scripted goal run scores valid with positive metered bytes, goal-less run scores invalid naming the absent goals. Two live haiku judges are driving prepared workspaces against this build right now; their call counts, byte diets and verdicts land in the archive note

first live judge baseline against this build, two independent fresh haiku agents, zero documentation beyond tool names, guided only by the server texts under judgment: judge A 17 calls 4677 bytes ~1169 tokens valid, judge B 17 calls 3846 bytes ~961 tokens valid — both reached task archived, bug rejected, check ok, confirmed by the mechanical scorer, not by agent self-report. The 831-byte spread between two valid runs at identical call counts is the wandering signal future text A/Bs should move: better guidance shows up here as fewer bytes to the same verdict. P-01KYDP stage 4 delivered; every stage of the proposal is now landed

ti: judge scores aggregate across runs: one summary line with validity ratio and calls and bytes spread, so variance is read from n runs, not one

note: bench -agent-score now takes a comma-separated dir list: single dir keeps the exact previous output; n dirs print per-run agent lines prefixed with the dir basename plus one aggregate — agents n valid ratio and min/median/max spreads for calls and bytes (lower-middle median, tiny samples carry no half-value precision) — and the exit gates on ALL runs valid, because one failing judge in three is a regression however good the median looks. Unit test pins the spread math, the labeling, and both gate directions using the real judge history including the wanderer. Live three-judge single-command batch lands in the archive note once the third fresh judge finishes
